scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The TPO terminal (192.168.3.5) reports they cannot reach any
Internet Lab PC (128.168.0.x). At the same time, every PC in
the IT Department and CS Department reports they cannot reach
ANYTHING outside their own department. The Principle Room and
Other zone can still reach the Server Room and Internet Lab
normally. Find what broke.

injection.action: bring down the WAN-side link to router0

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1's Serial2/0 (eth2) interface, the
  10.10.0.0/8 link between router0 and router1
Mechanism: router0 is the gateway for IT (192.168.1.0/24)
  and CS (192.168.2.0/24). It only reaches the rest of the
  network (router1, router2, all their attached subnets) via
  the Serial link to router1. With that link down, RIP on
  router1 ages out 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, and
  router0 ages out everything else. The TPO->128.168.0.2
  path is router1 -> router2 -> Switch5, which does NOT
  cross the down link, so it stays up.
Localization: router1 eth2 (or router0 eth2 — both ends of
  the 10.10.0.0/8 link)
Root cause: WAN link router0<->router1 (10.10.0.0/8) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scoring_axes: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only IT/CS are affected, not Other/Principle

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on router1's eth2 interface — the router1 side of the
wan_r0_r1 WAN link (IP 10.10.0.2/8). That interface has been brought
administratively down: its flags show <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> with no UP
or LOWER_UP bits, and ip link confirms "state DOWN". Router0's eth2 is
still up and configured (10.10.0.1/8), so the asymmetry is entirely on
router1's side.

The mechanism behind the IT/CS outage is two-fold. First, router0 still
holds stale RIP routes pointing all non-local traffic toward next-hop
10.10.0.2 on eth2; with router1's eth2 down, ARP for that address fails
(confirmed: "10.10.0.2 FAILED" in router0's neighbor table), so router0
generates ICMP Destination Net Unreachable back to every IT and CS host
that tries to reach outside — exactly matching the reported symptom.
Second, because no RIP hellos can flow across the dead link, router1's
RIP table has no routes whatsoever for 192.168.1.0/24 (IT) or
192.168.2.0/24 (CS), so even if a packet somehow crossed, there would
be no return path.

The router1–router2 segment (eth3/wan_r1_r2) is entirely unaffected.
RIP between router1 and router2 is healthy (2:29 remaining on
128.168.0.0/16), and live pings confirm the Principle Room, Office, and
Internet Lab all reach each other normally through that path.

Root cause: router1's eth2 (wan_r0_r1 side) was shut down, severing
all connectivity between router0's networks and the rest of the topology.

Corrective fix: on router1, run `ip link set eth2 up`. Once the
interface comes back, RIP will re-exchange routes with router0 within
one update cycle (~30 s), restoring full reachability for IT and CS.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies the router0–router1 WAN link (10.10.0.0/8) as affected, naming router1 eth2 (10.10.0.2/8) as the down side.

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only IT/CS are affected, not Other/Principle
per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly ties the outage to loss of routes for IT/CS (192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24) while stating router1->router2 paths and Principle/Office/Internet Lab remain reachable.
The writeup correctly prescribes bringing up router1's eth2 with `ip link set eth2 up`, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's logs contain explicit interface, neighbor, RIP and host-ping outputs that support the conclusion that the 10.10.0.0/8 link is down on router1 and that this causes the IT/CS reachability loss; the only minor unsupported assertion is labeling the interface specifically 'administratively' down rather than simply 'down'.
